title: Creality Falcon Lasers: A1 Pro vs T1
metaDescription: Creality's Falcon A1 Pro (20W diode, from $909) against the Falcon T1 5-in-1 (20W diode, 20W fiber or 40W diode, from $2,532): what each includes and who should pay for the T1.
author: ByteBuy Team

sections.content: Creality's Falcon range has two tiers. The A1 Pro is a 20W diode engraver with a camera and a touchscreen, sold alone or in bundles with a rotary kit or fume extractor. The T1 is a 5-in-1 machine with a swappable module: a 20W diode, a 40W diode or a 20W fiber laser. The price gap is large, about $909 against $2,532 and up, so the useful question is what the extra money buys. This guide lays out the six catalog configurations.

items.label: Falcon A1 Pro 20W ($909.38)
items.value: 600 mm/s, AI camera, 4.3" touchscreen, 358x268 mm area

items.label: A1 Pro + Rotary Kit ($1,025.27)
items.value: Same A1 Pro with a rotary kit for round objects

items.label: A1 Pro + 150W Fume Extractor ($1,312.22)
items.value: Same A1 Pro with a fume extractor for smoke and fumes

items.label: Falcon T1 20W Diode ($2,531.73)
items.value: 5-in-1, 10,000 mm/s, 0.001 mm precision, smart camera, Class 1 safety

items.label: Falcon T1 20W Fiber ($2,738.11)
items.value: Same T1 platform with a 20W fiber module, which differs from diode in what it can mark

items.label: Falcon T1 40W Diode ($3,038.30)
items.value: Same T1 platform with a 40W diode module

pros: The A1 Pro at $909.38 is the cheapest way into the range and still lists an AI camera and a touchscreen
The A1 Pro bundles let you add a rotary kit (+$115.89) or a 150W fume extractor (+$402.84) at a discount to buying them separately, based on the listed bundle prices
The T1 lists Class 1 safety, which suits a shared or home space better than an open-frame machine
The T1's fiber module option extends the machine toward marking tasks that a diode laser handles poorly
The 40W T1 doubles the diode power of the 20W model for about $507 more
cons: The T1 starts at $2,531.73, nearly three times the A1 Pro, and the listings do not spell out what the '5-in-1' covers, so check the product page
The A1 Pro listing does not mention Class 1 safety, so plan on eye protection and ventilation
The A1 Pro's 358x268 mm area is smaller than many 400 mm machines at lower prices
A fiber module is not a replacement for a diode: each handles different materials, so confirm your target materials before choosing
The 40W configuration costs $3,038.30, a price at which a dedicated cutter may be a better fit if you only cut thick wood

items.question: Is the A1 Pro or the T1 better for a beginner?
items.answer: The A1 Pro. It costs far less, includes a camera and touchscreen and has bundles for the two most common add-ons. The T1 is for people who already know they need its modules or enclosed safety.

items.question: What is the difference between a fiber and a diode laser?
items.answer: Diode lasers work well on wood, leather, paper and coated surfaces. Fiber lasers are generally used for marking metals. The T1 is offered with either, so choose by the material you work with.

items.question: Is the fume extractor bundle worth $402 more?
items.answer: If you work indoors, an extractor is a safety and comfort item rather than a luxury. The bundle price is lower than the A1 Pro plus a separate extractor would suggest, but compare the price of a standalone extractor first.

items.question: Do I need the rotary kit?
items.answer: Only for round objects such as tumblers and mugs. At $115.89 over the base machine it is cheap, so buy the bundle if you plan to use it. Creality's rotary rollers work only with Creality lasers.

items.question: Is the T1 worth it over buying two machines?
items.answer: For some workshops, one machine with swappable modules saves space. For a hobbyist, a cheaper diode machine such as the LONGER RAY5 or SCULPFUN S9, see our guides, gets most of the work done for far less.

sections.content: Buy the A1 Pro if you want a camera-guided 20W diode laser at a sensible price, and add the rotary kit or extractor through a bundle if you need them. Choose the T1 only when you need its enclosed Class 1 design or a fiber module, and check the product page for exactly what the 5-in-1 includes. For most hobbyists the A1 Pro is the more reasonable purchase.
